# SneakToken

> A model-selection desk for people who pay the invoice. Input, cached-input and output prices per 1M tokens (USD), each read off the provider's own pricing page and dated. Five buying channels. Self-hosting sizing and break-even maths.

Rules this site follows:
- A price is only published with four things attached: the channel it was quoted on, the processing tier, the date checked, and the source URL.
- If the provider's own page cannot be read, the price is left empty. No aggregator numbers, ever.
- No capability rankings. Only verifiable facts: context window, licence, modalities, tool calling, self-host feasibility.
- Nobody pays for placement.

## Pages
- / — three-question model picker
- /models.html — full library, filterable, with sources on every record
- /cost.html — monthly cost calculator + API vs GPU break-even calculator
- /buy.html — five buying channels + enterprise procurement checklist
- /deploy.html — VRAM estimator, serving engines, GPU rental rates
- /market.html — dated price-change log and current snapshot
- /method.html — methodology, what we refuse to publish, corrections policy

## Standing caveats
- Providers change pricing without notice. Confirm on their own page before committing budget.
- Output tokens are usually 3-5x input, and decide most invoices.
- Cached input can be 10-50x cheaper than input; it is the biggest lever for workloads with stable prefixes.
- Self-hosting only wins above a crossover volume, and only if the hardware can physically push that throughput.
